sentiment.rationale: The document reports a strong backward-looking quarter (EBIT of USD 1.3bn vs USD 177m a year ago), but full-year 2025 guidance is reaffirmed unchanged (underlying EBIT USD 0-3bn). Management explicitly flags increased macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty, revised container market volume growth down to -1% to 4%, and cautions that the outlook is subject to considerable uncertainties. The forward signal is flat: guidance held, not raised, with cautious language on the outlook.

summary.eps: Earnings per share of USD 74 (Q1 2024: USD 11).
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 guidance maintained: underlying EBITDA USD 6-9bn, underlying EBIT USD 0-3bn, free cash flow at least negative USD 3.0bn. Global container market volume growth revised to -1% to 4% (from around 4%). Red Sea disruption expected to last for the full year.
summary.margin: EBITDA margin 20.3% (12.9% in Q1 2024); EBIT margin 9.4% (1.4% in Q1 2024).
key_risks: Increased macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty impacting container volume growth and freight rates.
Trade war and political uncertainty in the US, with risk of recession.
US-China trade tensions causing 30-40% drop in China-US volumes in April.
Potential for further escalation of tariffs and broader trade war.
Red Sea disruption expected to continue for the full year, impacting network costs.
Significant new vessel deliveries (2m TEU in 2025) increasing supply-side pressure.
Uncertainty around the reopening of the Red Sea and its impact on supply-demand balance.
key_opportunities: Gemini network launch providing greater flexibility and reliability, with cost savings expectations unchanged.
Logistics & Services on track to 6% EBIT margin target, with continued operational improvements.
Terminals delivering strong results with high utilisation and storage revenue.
Geographically diversified portfolio reduces exposure to US-centric trade tensions.
Strong balance sheet (net cash USD 5.2bn) allows continued investment and shareholder returns.
New solutions (Lead Logistics, bonded solutions, customs services) to support customers navigating tariffs.

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: Management describes a 'solid delivery' but repeatedly emphasises 'increased macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty,' revises volume growth downward, and maintains guidance with explicit caution about the outlook.

evidence.quote: Revenue increased by 7.8% or USD 966m to USD 13.3bn (USD 12.4bn)

evidence.claim: Earnings per share was USD 74, up from USD 11 in Q1 2024.

evidence.quote: A.P. Moller - Maersk (Maersk) maintains its full-year 2025 guidance of underlying EBITDA of USD 6-9bn, underlying EBIT of USD 0-3bn and free cash flow of at least negative USD 3.0bn.

evidence.claim: Global container market volume growth forecast was revised down to -1% to 4%.
evidence.quote: The global container market volume growth has been revised to -1% to 4% given the increased macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.

evidence.claim: EBITDA margin was 20.3%, up from 12.9% in Q1 2024.
EBIT margin was 9.4%, up from 1.4% in Q1 2024.
Management tone is cautious, emphasising uncertainty.
evidence.quote: Maersk’s guidance for 2025 is subject to considerable macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties impacting container volume growth and freight rates.

evidence.claim: Red Sea disruption is expected to last for the full year.
evidence.quote: The disruption in the Red Sea is expected to continue throughout the rest of the year.

evidence.claim: US-China trade tensions caused a 30-40% drop in China-US volumes in April.
evidence.quote: China-US volumes (~5% of total) have dropped 30-40% in April as customers wait and see how tariff situation resolves itself

evidence.claim: Gemini network is on track to deliver reliability and cost savings.
evidence.quote: Within its first two months of operations, the Gemini network is on track to deliver the reliability and savings ambition once fully phased in.

evidence.claim: Logistics & Services EBIT margin improved to 4.1% and is on track to 6%.
evidence.quote: Logistics & Services was on track in Q1 2025 with the EBIT margin improving by 2.6 percentage points year-over-year to 4.1% (1.5%)

evidence.claim: Terminals delivered strong results with ROIC of 14.5%.
evidence.quote: Terminals achieved a strong EBIT of USD 394m (USD 300m), driven by significant volume growth, higher storage revenue and increased revenue per move. ... ROIC (LTM) increased to 14.5% (11.3%).

evidence.claim: The company has a strong balance sheet with net cash of USD 5.2bn.
evidence.quote: Net interest-bearing debt amounted to a net cash position of USD 5.2bn (a net cash position of USD 7.4bn at 31 December 2024)

evidence.claim: New vessel deliveries of 2m TEU are expected in 2025, increasing supply.
evidence.quote: On the supply side, growth remained elevated in Q1 2025 driven by significant deliveries. At the end of the quarter, the nominal fleet was 9.4% larger than at the same time in 2024
